status: Verified deterministic Core policy outcomes; human balance remains open
scope: Fresh revision-2 Lantern Landing and Ribbon Crossing; five-star fixed mixed supply, 24/25 occupied opening cells, 150000/220000 targets, causal multipliers 1 through 5.

source.checkout: Working tree, not a clean published commit
source.temporaryFiles: Harness, executable and raw output are disposable; policy definitions and summarized results are retained here.
source.laterCoreChanges: After this model executable was compiled, save validation added an early board-count guard, an allowed-family check and a minimum-light check for two-star clears. StoryChallenge extracted the unchanged palette values into a shared property; StarRecipe had comment indentation changes. The Core owner reports unchanged opening, supply, settling and award behavior, with current-source regression tests reproducing all four winning action/shower counts.

postModelInspection.note: These hashes identify the later inspected Core files, not the earlier compiled model executable.

execution.configuration: Optimized host executable compiling production Core sources directly; no app, simulator or native presentation.
execution.assertions: Every applied player or shower transaction checks exact score delta, valid committed save and JSON round-trip equality; shower receipts preserve the announced forecast. Each final replay equals its original opening.

policies.idle: Apply each shower without any player action.
policies.tap: Choose the ordinary legal group with the largest committed Core award; break equal-point ties by larger group count, then first enumeration. Repeat until no group remains.
policies.eager: Compare tap choices with all right/up adjacent occupied swaps that immediately award points, using the same point/count tie break. If no rewarding action exists, choose one adjacent occupied swap enabling the highest-award ordinary tap, then re-evaluate. Different identities with the same family and grown state are skipped. No empty-cell swaps, traces or forecast lookahead.
policies.buffer: Use the eager choice. Stop acting until the next shower if that choice is a tap or setup swap, occupied count is at most 16, and tallest column is below 6. Immediately rewarding swaps remain eligible. This threshold is a policy assumption, not an adaptive supply rule.

measurements.showers: Committed shower count at the final win/loss, including the blocked shower for a loss.
measurements.actions: Taps plus immediately rewarding recipe swaps plus non-rewarding setup swaps. Showers are excluded.
measurements.occupancy: Occupied physical cells after the policy finishes its actions and before the next shower; each such boundary is sampled once. This is not time-weighted occupancy. A grown star still occupies one cell.
measurements.maxPreShowerHeight: Tallest occupied column at sampled boundaries; this is not a within-animation height measurement.
measurements.phaseCounts: Histogram of resolution-phase count for each player transaction, plus shower transactions with a nonempty resolution. Zero-phase entries are setup swaps; empty shower transactions are omitted.
measurements.score: Exact displayed points, including size and causal-combo bonuses.
measurements.time: No human elapsed time, reaction time, pauses or animation duration was modeled. Shower counts must not be presented as measured round durations.

independentPrototypeComparison.engine: A separate temporary Python reconstruction explored recipe-free openings and fixed mixed waves of 3, 5 and 6 stars before the production Core run.
independentPrototypeComparison.status: Design exploration only; its measurements are not substituted for the production Core results above.
independentPrototypeComparison.decision: Prototype five-star waves. They fit the existing maximum shower size and supported both winning policies in actual Core. Six stars would expand the rule/save contract and did not establish a sufficient density benefit in the independent exploration.
independentPrototypeComparison.limits: Three- and six-star variants were not adopted or executed by the production Core harness.

findings: All four eager/buffer runs win; both idle runs overflow on shower 5 at zero score. The fixed supply does not passively finish these openings.
Both tap-only runs lose before target. These examples establish recoverability with simple swaps, not that every casual strategy succeeds.
Buffer policies average about 13.4/13.5 occupied cells; eager policies average about 5.2/7.2. A half-full opening does not guarantee sustained half-full or quarter-full play.
The buffered Lantern run needs 24 actions and Ribbon 46; eager runs need 52 and 88. These are specific deterministic policies, not best-play bounds or measured player effort.
openAcceptance: Human judgment of useful choices, waiting, difficulty and recoverable Lantern mistakes.
Native entry/cascade readability, input timing, sound, motion and accessibility evidence owned by the accompanying report.
Phone play and canonical installation are separate from these host-Core results.
